I would keep my 58.1 mu split across all four crops so I do not put the whole year on one market or one weather risk. I have 20 years of experience and I have well irrigation, so I would lean on crops I can manage reliably rather than chasing the highest-risk return. I would keep winter wheat on the more stable land because it gives me grain and cash earlier, then follow part of that land with summer maize because that rotation fits local practice and spreads labor. I would keep stevia as the main cash crop because it matches my current cropping direction, but I would not put all land into it because it needs tighter field management and market confidence. I would keep some cotton because it still fits my experience and spreads pest and price risk. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it matters most, keep fertilizer at moderate-to-strong levels because I have irrigation to support it, and avoid extreme input use. I would plough for wheat and cotton where I want a cleaner, deeper seedbed, and use rotary tillage for maize and stevia to save time and labor. I would plan for steady irrigation and a practical number of pesticide sprays, aiming for dependable yield instead of the absolute maximum.
